issues.problem: "Je ne veux pas quelque chose seulement pour les touristes." is ungrammatical or at best clumsy French. Standard French doesn't put "quelque chose" after a negation; it uses "rien" or "pas de". "Seulement pour" also sounds stilted for "just for". The same sentence is repeated in the speaking opener, so learners would rehearse the error.
issues.suggestedFix: Use "Je ne veux pas un plat pour touristes." or "Je ne veux rien de spécial pour les touristes." (closest to the neutral "algo": "Je ne veux pas de truc juste pour les touristes." if a casual register is acceptable). Put the same wording in speaking.openingFrench.

issues.problem: The roles are inverted. The opener is the learner's own lines: the question about local breakfast plus the line refusing tourist food. If it is the partner's opening turn, the server is asking the learner's questions. Either way, objectives 1 and 2 are already done before the learner speaks.
issues.suggestedFix: Give the opening to the server, e.g. "Bonjour ! Qu'est-ce que je vous sers ce matin ?". Have the learner then do objectives 1–5. If the schema allows, add an explicit role field (partnerRole: "le serveur", learnerRole: "Ana / la cliente").

issues.problem: The See answer is the whole card face including the parenthetical gloss: "le café de olla (café à la cannelle, préparé dans une cruche en terre)". No learner can reproduce that gloss exactly, so answer-checking fails. "Cruche" is also the wrong word: it means a jug or pitcher, while an olla is a clay pot.
issues.suggestedFix: Set cards[6].fr to "le café de olla". Move the gloss to a separate note or glossFrench field: "café préparé à la cannelle (et souvent au piloncillo) dans un pot en terre cuite". Set modes[0].targetFrench to "le café de olla".

issues.problem: The Type answer "la salsa (la sauce)" puts parentheses inside a string the learner must type. Exact-match checking will reject correct answers.
issues.suggestedFix: Set cards[4].fr to "la salsa" and add "la sauce" as an accepted alternative (acceptedFrench: ["la salsa", "la sauce"]). Set modes[3].targetFrench to "la salsa".

issues.problem: The cue asks the learner to "Read the script line: a server asks if you want a recommendation", but the mode has no script line. The flow is also illogical: if the server offers a recommendation, the learner answering "Pouvez-vous me recommander un plat typique ?" makes little sense. And the activity is English→French production, so it doesn't test hearing at all.
issues.suggestedFix: Add a scriptFrench field holding the source-linked French line ("Pouvez-vous me recommander un plat typique ?"). Make Hear a comprehension task: read or hear the script, then pick or write the English ("Can you recommend a typical dish to me?"). Keep scriptOnly: true and sourceCardIndex 13.

issues.path: modes[0], modes[3], modes[5] (See/Type/Write); modes[1] vs modes[4] (Recall/Say)
issues.problem: The modes aren't really different from each other. See, Type and Write are all "English → produce French". Recall ("say the French") is a speaking task, while Say is reading French aloud. So the answer is shown in the cue, and the speaking behaviour sits in Recall, not in Say.
issues.suggestedFix: See: show the French card face and ask for the English meaning (recognition). Recall: English cue → produce French from memory (written). Type: English → typed French term. Say: English cue → say the French (script-only, with targetFrench hidden from the cue). Write: full-sentence production. Update the instructionEnglish strings to match.

issues.problem: "ce qu'il contient" has no antecedent on a standalone card. In the Reader, the line before mentions "les chilaquiles" (plural), so a singular "il" reads as an agreement error. Spanish "qué lleva" has a null subject. "Contenir" is also more formal than a spoken restaurant question.
issues.suggestedFix: Use "Pouvez-vous m'expliquer ce qu'il y a dedans ?" in both cards[14].fr and reader.french[5] (and modes[4].targetFrench). Alternative: "…ce que contient ce plat ?".

issues.problem: "morceaux de tortilla frits dans la salsa" says the tortilla pieces are fried in the salsa, which is wrong: they are fried first, then simmered or coated in salsa. The gloss also makes the answer face too long to recall.
issues.suggestedFix: Use "les chilaquiles" as the face, with the gloss moved to a note: "morceaux de tortilla frits, nappés de salsa".

issues.problem: "le café de olla est servi avec de la cannelle" suggests cinnamon on the side. Spanish "va con canela" here means it is made with cinnamon (brewed in).
issues.suggestedFix: Use "Le serveur explique que le café de olla est préparé à la cannelle et que le pan dulce est pour après."

verdict: NOT READY. Mechanical parity passes: 16 cards with exact en/es/kind in order, 9 English and 9 Spanish Reader lines identical to the source, all six modes' sourceEnglish and targetFrench match their indexed cards, the four forms align with the source verbs and English examples, lessonId core:7 is kept, all eight gates are false, and the old.json Lyon/tartines drift has not come back. Blocking problems: an ungrammatical French card that is reused in the speaking opener; a speaking opener with inverted roles; a false 'written fresh' provenance note; and mode answers with parenthetical glosses that can't be checked. Mode design and the gloss accuracy (cruche, frits dans la salsa, servi avec de la cannelle) also need fixes. This is an unqualified automated critique only. It is not a qualified French review and does not approve anything.
